speaker: N
text: In 1902, a city paid people to kill rats, and ended up with more rats than ever.

speaker: N
text: The city was Hanoi, and its shiny new sewers had become a highway for rats.

speaker: N
text: Rats popped out of toilets in the fanciest homes in town.

speaker: N
text: So the officials made a simple offer.

speaker: N
text: Bring us a rat tail, and we'll pay you one cent.

speaker: N
text: Tails poured in by the thousands.

speaker: N
text: Some days, more than twenty thousand of them.

speaker: N
text: The officials cheered, counting tails in big wooden crates.

speaker: N
text: But the streets were still crawling.

speaker: N
text: And people started noticing something odd.

speaker: N
text: Rats were running around with no tails.

speaker: N
text: Meanwhile, outside the city, inspectors found barns full of rats, fed and cared for like pets.

speaker: N
text: You see, the city wasn't paying for dead rats.

speaker: N
text: It was paying for tails.

speaker: N
text: And a rat doesn't need its tail to make more rats.

speaker: N
text: So clever hunters caught a rat, snipped off its tail, and let it go.

speaker: N
text: Every rat they freed had babies, and every baby grew a brand new tail.

speaker: N
text: Some people stopped hunting altogether and simply farmed them.

speaker: N
text: The more the city paid, the more rats it got.

speaker: N
text: Economists call this a perverse incentive.

speaker: N
text: When you reward the proof instead of the result, people just make more proof.

speaker: N
text: Hanoi quietly cancelled the bounty.

speaker: N
text: Which is the real story of how...
